svg.text: MPx Spin: Hand-Crank Centrifugal Filter
Turn the crank and the basket spins. Spinning throws the water outward through a steel-mesh + organic sleeve, which keeps the microplastics. No electricity, and the sleeve lifts out for replacement.
Concept sketch · v0.1
A · The unit
pour · crank · pour out · swap
Works like a salad spinner, but the water is what passes through: the spin pushes it
through the sleeve, and the plastic particles stay behind on the sleeve's inner face.

stain it with Nile Red and count the plastics

D · Using it, and whether the physics works
Why spinning works as a pump

g.text: Spinning water presses outward. The pressure at the wall is roughly
(ρ water density, ω spin rate, r basket radius)
• 600 rpm → about 7 kPa (like 0.7 m of water pushing down)
• 900 rpm → about 16 kPa (like 1.6 m of water)
A hand turns about 120–180 rpm; the 1:5 gear gives 600–900 rpm.
Pressure drops as the basket empties, so keep cranking to the end.

svg.text: CHECK BEFORE BUILDING

g.text: The 0.5 mm mesh is only a support. It stops pieces
over 0.5 mm; the organic sleeve does the fine filtering.
Fine sleeves clog. Test flow against pore size to
find how often a sleeve needs changing.
Light plastics (PE, PP) drift inward when spun, but
the water flowing out still carries them to the sleeve.
Don't add plastic by accident. Keep the gears above
the water; use steel, glass and ceramic in the wet parts.
No germ treatment here (no power for UV). Pair it
with a UV stage or boil the water if germs are a concern.

svg.text: Pressure figures are estimates from the formula,
not measurements; a prototype test should confirm them.
Sources

g.text: [1] Rermborirak et al. (2025). Low-cost portable microplastic detection system integrating Nile Red fluorescence staining with YOLOv8-based deep learning (FLOro). J. Hazard. Mater. Adv. 19, 100787. Used 11 µm filter paper.
[2] Wang, H., Dai, S. et al. (2023). Microplastics removal in the aquatic environment via fungal pelletization. Bioresource Technology Reports.
